links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers with vs without retrieval grounding (GraphRAG/DocRAG vs Vanilla) on fluid therapy questions
links.effect: GraphRAG accuracy 96.89% MCQ / 66.44% open-ended vs Vanilla 69.44%/27.56%; case-based 71.12% GraphRAG, 62.47% DocRAG vs 52.67% Vanilla.
links.quote: On the retrospective case-based question set, GraphRAG also showed the strongest overall performance, with an average accuracy of 71.12%, compared with 62.47% for DocRAG, 54.20% for CoT, 52.67% for Vanilla, and 52.54% for RoT.

links.outcome: Rate of explicit uncertainty acknowledgment ('Don't Know') with option added and with RAG
links.effect: Adding a 'Don't Know' option raised abstention from 2.68% to 20.01%; GraphRAG raised 'Don't Know' rate from 17.86% to 35.00%.
links.quote: As shown in Fig 4 , adding a “Don’t Know” option substantially increased the proportion of honest abstention responses from 2.68% to 20.01%, suggesting that explicit uncertainty choices reduced the tendency to guess when the model was unsure.

links.outcome: Rater independence, blinding, and adjudication procedures for grading LLM responses
links.effect: Two clinicians independently rated with consensus for disagreements, but no formal blinded model-identity masking, no inter-rater agreement analysis; single nurse human baseline.
links.quote: Fourth, open-ended responses were evaluated using binary expert judgment without formal blinded model-identity masking, which may introduce assessment bias.

links.outcome: Representativeness and independence of test data from retrieval knowledge base
links.effect: Knowledge-based questions and retrieval used the same PFTKG knowledge space, limiting external generalization; case-based set from a single hospital.
links.quote: In the knowledge-based evaluation setting, question construction and retrieval were both based on the same PFTKG knowledge space.

links.outcome: LLM strategies compared against each other and an exploratory nurse baseline
links.effect: Nurse achieved 93% MCQ and 90% open-ended; GraphRAG comparable on MCQ (96.89%) but nurse exceeded all LLM configurations on open-ended (best 66.44%).
links.quote: Her multiple-choice performance was comparable to the best-performing LLM strategy, whereas her open-ended performance exceeded all tested LLM configurations.

links.outcome: Claude refusal or redirect behavior on clinical case questions
links.effect: 73.26% of Claude's incorrect responses on case-based questions began with a refusal-style phrase, lowering its measured accuracy.
links.quote: Specifically, 73.26% of Claude’s incorrect responses began with the refusal-style phrase “I appreciate you reaching out, but I need to clarify my role and limitations.

links.effect: Average accuracy was 75.16% for multiple-choice and 35.71% for open-ended questions.
links.quote: Across all LLMs and prompting strategies, accuracy was markedly higher for multiple-choice questions than for open-ended questions (average 75.16% vs. 35.71% ).

links.effect: Knowledge-set GraphRAG reached 96.89% MCQ/66.44% open-ended; case-based overall accuracy was 71.12%.
links.quote: Performance on case-based question set was lower than on the knowledge-based question set, which is expected because case-based questions require more context-sensitive judgment under clinically grounded conditions.

unlisted_practices: Use GraphRAG with a clinical knowledge graph, hierarchical community detection, recursive summarization, and finding-level retrieval rather than document-level RAG.
Select community detection algorithms for GraphRAG using modularity and average communitude, with sensitivity analysis of alternative algorithms.
